angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 937,107.9 km at 122.78 pc = 0.071 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is published; the disc is far too small to resolve.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.1443 +/- 0.0116 mas (photometry/gaia-dr3-source.csv), no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius: 1.347 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius, the stellar radius '[f]rom TESS data' in the Challener, Weiner Mansfield et al. (2025), Nature Astronomy (arXiv:2510.24708), deposited ThERESA configuration wasp-18b-3d-8bin-sinusoidal-tiovo.cfg in Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14751570; with its semi-major axis of 0.02180079 au it gives the a/R* of 3.48023 the Eigenspectra maps were fitted with. GM from the same file's stellar mass, 1.5596 solar masses, times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2. presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the star's spin axis is not measured in three dimensions.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Cortes-Zuleta et al. (2020), A&A 636, A98: 6,432 +/- 48 K, the stellar temperature Coulombe et al. (2023, Nature 620, 292, Methods) convert WASP-18b's maps with (https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08192)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-18 (pscomppars): spectral type F6 IV-V, from Salz et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015A&A...576A..42S/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 10069: main object type SB*, Spectroscopic Binary
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-18 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.107 dex, from Cortés-Zuleta et al. 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...636A..98C/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-18 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.42813, from Cortés-Zuleta et al. 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...636A..98C/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-18 (pscomppars): age 1.57 Gyr, from Cortés-Zuleta et al. 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...636A..98C/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/A+A/684/A28/tablea1 (Evolution of lithium in FGK dwarfs), column Prot: 0.891369 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place. The middle of 2 catalogued periods, 2 of them within 20% of it
